results.content:
What reviewers repeatedly criticize:

 The mobile app. The most common complaint by a wide margin — sluggish, feature-incomplete relative to web, occasional sync lag.
 Notification volume. Poll participants get emailed on every response by default. On a 15-person poll, that's a lot of inbox noise attributed to you.
 Support response times. Recurring theme on lower-star reviews, particularly for free and Pro users.
 Feature gating. Several things that feel basic — removing branding, custom reminders — sit behind Pro.
 UI churn. Long-time users complain about redesigns moving familiar controls.

Read the one-star reviews before the five-star ones. On Doodle, the negative reviews cluster around mobile and support, not the core product. That is a good sign about the core product. [...] TL;DR

 Doodle's free tier still works for one-off group polls, but it carries ads and strips branding — fine internally, awkward with prospects.
 Paid plans jump sharply between monthly and annual billing. Annual costs about half the monthly rate. That gap is where most "Doodle is expensive" complaints come from.
 Reviewers consistently praise the group-poll UX and consistently criticize the mobile app, the notification volume, and support responsiveness.
 Doodle is a scheduling tool, not a pipeline tool. It does nothing about who you're scheduling with — that's a data problem, not a calendar problem.
 If your booking rate is low, the bottleneck is almost never the scheduler. It's bad contact data and a weak first touch.

## What is Doodle, and who actually uses it?# [...] ## What do Doodle reviews actually say?#

Pull the aggregate review data from G2 and Capterra and a consistent pattern shows up. Doodle scores well overall — typically in the 4.3–4.6 range across thousands of reviews — but the distribution of what people praise and criticize is unusually tight.

What reviewers repeatedly praise:

 Zero-friction participation. Recipients don't need an account. For external scheduling, this is the whole ballgame.
 The poll format itself. No competitor has meaningfully beaten Doodle at "find a time for nine people."
 Speed. Creating a poll takes under a minute. Reviewers mention this more than any feature.
 Calendar sync reliability. Once connected, availability updates are generally trusted.
